scenario: Everything went wrong on Tuesday: it rained, the coffee machine broke, and the team missed an important call because it was booked in the wrong room. The next day they play the 'what if' game, so the episode is full of third conditionals and 'wish + past perfect'. Kate: 'If Den had checked the calendar, we wouldn't have missed the call.' Den: 'If it hadn't rained, I would have walked to work.' Alex: 'If I had gone to bed earlier, I wouldn't have been so tired.' Pol: 'If the machine hadn't broken, we could have had coffee.' Peter: 'I wish I had set two alarms.' Kate ends warmly: 'If only we had known — but we learned a lot.' Nobody blames anyone; it's affectionate hindsight. Use clear third conditionals ('If + past perfect, would/could/might have + past participle') and 'I wish / if only + past perfect'. Short B1 sentences.
